prize_parts.citation: for a visionary body of prose and poetry in which memory, the body and metaphysical speculation are built into an expansive, densely patterned imaginative architecture

statement.case_for: My opening view holds: Cărtărescu's case rests on voice, formal ambition and sustained imaginative depth, not on any outside factor. Blinding and Solenoid fuse memory, the body and metaphysical speculation into one recognizable system, and the lyric background shapes the prose texture. The project looks cumulative and self-renewing across decades, not a single peak. A whole-oeuvre citation is easy to attribute to one writer, and it can rest on the large visionary novel with the poetry as a related strand. Colleagues' agreement is not an argument and I give it no weight. I tested the case against the strongest rival cases in the openings, and it still compares well on distinctiveness and scale of achievement.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that the prose achievement depends on dense Romanian patterning, wordplay and rhythm, which I can judge only through translation and public reception. Even the translated corpus covers the poetry and early work unevenly. The recursion of motifs across very long books can be read as depth or as insularity and excess. If the committee cannot establish that the style survives translation, a case this dependent on linguistic texture is less secure than it looks.

responses.point: Michon's compressed, rhythmically exact French turns obscure lives and art history into narrative inquiry. Palm sees very high linguistic and formal achievement, but a slim corpus that raises a breadth question.
responses.response: I agree that Michon's concentration of language is among the strongest on the list, and I ranked him seventh only on the criterion of sustained, broad achievement, not on quality of sentence. Palm names the same tension I feel, which is that quality over volume is a real strength but the body of work offers limited evidence of range. The translation loss is also heavy for a style built on syntax and cadence. I keep him below Cărtărescu, but I accept that someone who weights intensity over scale could reasonably place him higher.

responses.point: Can Xue's dream-logic fiction destabilizes psychology, space and causality with sustained rigor and few parallels in contemporary world literature. Sward's main uncertainty is the limited translated corpus.
responses.response: I did not rank Can Xue among my top eight, and I can say why without dismissing the case. The method is unmistakable, but I cannot judge from the translated selection whether it develops across the oeuvre or repeats, and Sward's own doubt about translation coverage points to the same gap. A prize cannot rest on a corpus I cannot assess, so I would want that coverage question settled before I moved her up. Sward's point that the strangeness has internal rigor is fair, and it is why I regard this as an open question rather than a weakness.

responses.point: Zurita's large poetic sequences and landscape-scale interventions turn historical suffering into collective memorial form. Olsson ranked him second, while noting the difficulty of judging non-textual work as literature.
responses.response: I ranked Zurita eighth, and I disagree with Olsson mainly about weight. The ambition and the coherence of the project are clear. But poetry in translation is the least secure basis for judgment, and the interventions beyond the page and the strong political and historical context make it hard to isolate the language itself. Olsson names that same difficulty. I would need a close account of the poems on the page before treating the scale of the project as literary achievement.

responses.point: Murnane's radically inward, formally rigorous fiction builds real philosophical depth from a severely limited method. Mattson ranked him third, while noting how narrow the thematic range is.
responses.response: I ranked Murnane sixth and share the admiration for his singular voice and consistency of method. The question is whether narrowness is a discipline or a ceiling. A deliberately self-contained project can show remarkable depth, but it gives thinner evidence of significance across a body of work than a writer whose project keeps widening. Mattson's observation that the late work extends the early method supports durability but not range, so I stay at sixth.

responses.point: Carson's unmistakable voice and formal invention across genres are real. Sem-Sandberg asks whether genre-crossing and partly object-based works are best judged as an oeuvre in the sense of Nobel's will.
responses.response: That is the question that keeps Carson second for me and not first. I find the formal invention and the classical depth convincing, and I see Autobiography of Red and Nox as lasting. But some of the effect lies in book design and in translation and scholarship at the edge of an original oeuvre. A citation would have to define the scope carefully, probably around poetry and lyric-essayistic renewal. I think that is possible, which is why I name her as an alternative, but it needs more articulation than the Cărtărescu case does.

uncertainties: How well Cărtărescu's dense Romanian prose and poetry survive translation, and how complete the translated corpus is, is not independently verified and I have not claimed to have read the texts.
Whether the recurrence of motifs across his long books is sustained depth or self-repetition remains open to differing readings.
For Carson, how a committee would weigh hybrid, object-based and translated work within an oeuvre-based citation under Nobel's will is unresolved.
For Yan Lianke, the effect of translation and censorship context on reception has to be separated from literary assessment, and quality across the large output is uneven in public discussion.
My own voting status as a co-opted member is undocumented, so her simulated vote is a modeling assumption.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. My own work is non-fiction and biography, and nothing in the profile connects me to any shortlisted writer.
